renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: contig_feature_scatter
  title: Features against contig length
  description: |-
    Each point is a contig: its length on the horizontal axis and the number of features the four screens put on it on the vertical axis, sized by feature density and coloured by the screen with the most features there. It answers which contigs carry an unusual load of resistance genes, peptides, clusters or CAZymes.
    How to read: long contigs carry more of everything, so the interesting points are the short contigs high on the plot, which are dense loci. A contig with features from several screens is a candidate for a mobile or multi-function element, so open the screening tabs for it.
    Note: length is read from the contig name when the assembler wrote it there, so contigs without it are not drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Contig length (bp)
    y_title: Features on the contig
    log_x: true
  roles:
    x: contig_length
    y: features
    label: contig
    color: top_screen
    size: features_per_kb

- component: figure
  title: Feature density per contig
  description: |-
    Each bar counts contigs in a bin of feature density (features per kilobase), split by the screen with the most features on the contig. It answers how dense the annotated loci are and which screen drives the dense ones.
    How to read: most contigs sit at low density, and a long right tail marks dense loci such as resistance islands. A tail made of one screen shows which screen produces the dense contigs.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the 95th percentile of the feature density of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of funcscan.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: features_per_kb
    color: top_screen
    labels:
      features_per_kb: Features per kb
      top_screen: Top screen
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: p95
    column: features_per_kb

- component: card
  title: Features by screen
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of features the four screens put on the contigs and the bars rank the screens by the features on the contigs they lead. It answers which screen annotates the most loci.
    How to read: the screens differ by orders of magnitude in what they report, so a screen at the top reflects its design as much as the data.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  column: features
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: top_screen
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: features, by leading screen

- component: card
  title: Contigs by leading screen
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of contigs that carry at least one feature and the ring splits them by the screen with the most features on each. It answers which screen annotates most contigs.
    How to read: a ring held by one screen means the others find little on these contigs. Open the screening tabs to see which tools report the features.
  column: contig
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: top_screen
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: contigs, by leading screen

- component: card
  title: Contig length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median length of the annotated contigs and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how contiguous the assembly is where the features sit.
    How to read: a metagenome assembly is mostly short contigs with a long tail of long ones. Contigs without the length in their name are left out.
  column: contig_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: contig length across contigs

- component: card
  title: Screens per contig
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average number of screens (resistance genes, peptides, clusters and CAZymes) that put a feature on the same contig, out of the four the pipeline runs. It answers how often the screens find features on the same locus.
    How to read: every contig in the table carries at least one screen, so an average near 1 means almost every contig is annotated by one screen only. Higher values point to loci with several functions, which are worth a look.
    Lines and annotations: the dial maximum is four, the number of screens nf-core/funcscan runs.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  column: screens_on_contig
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 4.0
  caption: screens per contig, out of four

- component: card
  title: Feature density
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average number of features per kilobase on the annotated contigs and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how densely the screens annotate a contig.
    How to read: an average well above the median means a few very dense contigs pull it up. Open the scatter to find them.
  column: features_per_kb
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: density across contigs

- component: table
  title: Annotated contigs table
  description: |-
    Each row is a contig that carries at least one feature, with its length and coverage when the name holds them, the features from each screen, the screens on the contig and the feature density. It answers the exact numbers behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by feature density to list the densest loci.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: contig

- component: table
  title: Input samplesheet
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and the assembly it was screened from. It answers which inputs the run used.
    How to read: check that every expected sample is listed with its assembly path.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: screen_scatter
  title: Resistance genes against CAZymes
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample: its resistance gene hits on the horizontal axis and its CAZyme genes on the vertical axis, sized by biosynthetic gene cluster regions and coloured by antimicrobial peptide candidates. It answers how the four screens compare across samples.
    How to read: both counts grow with assembly size, so a sample far from the cloud is either unusually resistant or unusually poorly assembled. A lasso selection filters the rest of the dashboard to those samples.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    color_col: amp_candidates
    x_title: Resistance gene hits
    y_title: CAZyme genes
  roles:
    x: arg_hits
    y: cazymes
    label: sample
    size: bgc_regions

- component: figure
  id: screen_composition
  title: Findings per screen and sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is the number of findings one screen (resistance genes, peptide candidates, cluster regions or CAZymes) made in a sample, on a log axis, grouped by screen. It answers how the four screens compare within and between samples.
    How to read: the screens differ by orders of magnitude, so read the log axis rather than the bar heights. A screen missing from a sample returned nothing there, which can mean it was not enabled.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  code: |-
    # The colour channel belongs to the screen here, so the dashboard's
    # analysis groups take the facet axis instead: one band of samples per
    # group. Spread into the reshape below too, or the unpivot would drop the
    # annotation column before the facet could read it.
    index_cols = ["sample"] + [c for c in depictio_group_by if c != "sample"]
    grp_col = depictio_group_by[0] if depictio_group_by else None
  
    # wide -> long so each screen becomes its own bar colour
    df_modified = df.unpivot(
        index=index_cols,
        on=["arg_hits", "amp_candidates", "bgc_regions", "cazymes"],
        variable_name="screen",
        value_name="findings",
    ).filter(pl.col("findings") > 0)
  
    labels = {
        "arg_hits": "ARG hits",
        "amp_candidates": "AMP candidates",
        "bgc_regions": "BGC regions",
        "cazymes": "CAZymes",
    }
    df_modified = df_modified.with_columns(
        pl.col("screen").replace_strict(labels, default=pl.col("screen")).alias("screen")
    )
  
    fig = px.bar(
        df_modified.to_pandas(),
        x="sample",
        y="findings",
        color="screen",
        barmode="group",
        log_y=True,
        facet_col=grp_col,
        category_orders={"screen": list(labels.values())},
    )
    fig.update_layout(
        yaxis_title="Findings (log scale)",
        legend_title_text="Screen",
        margin={"t": 24, "l": 56, "r": 16, "b": 80},
    )
    if grp_col:
        # Each panel keeps only its own samples, and its title is the group
        # name rather than the annotation column's name and an equals sign.
        fig.update_xaxes(matches=None, showticklabels=True, title_text="")
        fig.for_each_annotation(lambda a: a.update(text=a.text.split("=")[-1]))
    else:
        fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="Sample")

- component: card
  title: Resistance gene hits
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of resistance gene hits over all samples and the box shows their quartiles per sample. It answers how large the resistome is and how evenly the samples share it.
    How to read: a wide box means some samples carry far more resistance genes than others. Hits are counted per tool, so one gene found by several tools counts several times.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  column: arg_hits
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: hits per sample, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Distinct resistance genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of distinct resistance genes per sample and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how rich a typical resistome is.
    How to read: compare it with the hits card, since many hits on few genes mean the same genes are found by several tools or repeated in the assembly.
  column: arg_genes
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distinct genes per sample

- component: card
  title: Peptide candidates
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of antimicrobial peptide candidates per sample and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how many candidates a typical sample yields.
    How to read: candidates are predictions, not validated peptides, so a high count calls for the confidence column in the table before follow-up.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  column: amp_candidates
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: candidates per sample, with their spread

- component: card
  title: High-confidence peptide candidates
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of peptide candidates whose best prediction score reaches the AMPcombi cut-off, and the histogram shows how many each sample has. It answers how many candidates are strong enough to follow up.
    How to read: a sample with many candidates and few above the cut-off carries mostly weak predictions. Compare it with the candidates card.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is a prediction score of 0.6, the default of the nf-core/funcscan parameter amp_ampcombi_parsetables_cutoff, below which AMPcombi sets a score to 0 in its summary. The pipeline does not call this high confidence, so the name is the dashboard's.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: amp_high_confidence
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: high-confidence candidates per sample

- component: card
  title: Biosynthetic gene cluster regions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of biosynthetic gene cluster regions found and the ring splits them by sample. It answers which samples hold the secondary metabolite potential.
    How to read: regions are predicted from the assembly, so a poorly assembled sample can show fewer. A ring held by one sample points to a metagenome with a dominant producer.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  column: bgc_regions
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: regions, by sample

- component: card
  title: Cluster product classes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest count of distinct biosynthetic product classes in a sample and the histogram shows the distribution over samples. It answers how diverse the cluster repertoire is.
    How to read: a sample with many classes holds a broad secondary metabolite repertoire. Compare it with the region count, since many regions of few classes mean repeated clusters.
  column: bgc_classes
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: product classes per sample

- component: card
  title: CAZyme genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of carbohydrate-active enzyme genes per sample and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how much carbohydrate degradation capacity a typical sample has.
    How to read: the count grows with assembly size, so compare samples of similar assemblies. A sample far above the box is a candidate for a specialised degrader.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  column: cazymes
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: genes per sample, with their spread

- component: card
  title: CAZyme families
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average count of distinct CAZyme families per sample and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how varied the enzyme repertoire is.
    How to read: many genes of few families mean repeated enzymes, and many families mean a broad repertoire.
  column: cazyme_families
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: families per sample

- component: table
  title: Screening hub table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its headline counts for every screen: resistance gene hits and distinct genes, peptide candidates and those at the cut-off, cluster regions and classes, and CAZyme genes and families. It answers the exact numbers behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by a column to rank the samples, and select a row to filter the other tabs.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: figure
  title: Tools per screen
  description: |-
    Each bar is a screen of the pipeline (resistance, peptides, clusters, CAZymes or shared steps), stacked by the tools the run recorded for it. It answers which tools each screen ran.
    How to read: a screen with a single tool is a thin check, and one with many tools cross-validates its calls. Compare it with the findings in the screening tabs.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: screen
    y: tools
    color: tool
    labels:
      screen: Screen
      tools: Tools
      tool: Tool

- component: card
  title: Tools in the run
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct tools the run recorded and the bars rank the screens by how many each used. It answers how many tools the run drew on.
    How to read: the count depends on which screens and tools were enabled, so a lower number than expected points to skipped tools.
  column: tool
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: screen
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: tools, by screen

- component: card
  title: Processes by screen
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of process and tool records and the ring splits them by screen. It answers how the workflow is divided between the screens.
    How to read: a large share for a screen means many steps (downloads, summaries, conversions) beside the tool itself.
  column: process
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: screen
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: process records, by screen

- component: card
  title: Tool records by screen
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of tool version records and the bar shows the share each screen holds. It answers which screens carry the most software.
    How to read: a tool recorded in several processes appears several times, so the share reflects usage as well as variety.
  column: tool
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: screen
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: tool records, by screen

- component: card
  title: Versions in the run
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct version strings the run recorded and the bars rank the tools by how many versions each reports. It answers whether any tool ran in more than one version.
    How to read: one version per tool is the normal case. A tool with two versions means mixed containers, which hurts reproducibility, so compare it with the table.
  column: version
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: tool
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: versions, by tool

- component: table
  title: Software versions table
  description: |-
    Each row is a process and tool with the version the run recorded, and the screen the process belongs to. It answers the exact software the results came from.
    How to read: filter by screen or tool, and cite the versions in a methods section.
